item.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. item.title: Police confirm escape of two convicted inmates from Kogi prison
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has confirmed the escape of two convicted inmates from the Okene Correctional Centre, saying efforts are underway to apprehend them. The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. According to Afusat, the inmates escaped from the correctional facility on Sunday, November 8, at about 10:30 a.m. She said the command received a report from the correctional centre and was collaborating with the Nigerian Correctional Service and other relevant security agencies to ensure the prompt rearrest of the escapees. The police spokesperson added that efforts to trace and apprehend the fleeing inmates were ongoing. Afusat also clarified that the statement was her first and only official communication to the press on the incident. She urged members of the public to disregard any other information or publication attributed to her on the matter unless officially confirmed by the police command. item.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
item.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old. Vanguard News The post 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway

item.title: Only 36% of Nigerians have access to improved toilets — FG
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. He listed the initiatives to include capacity building for Environmental Health Officers on faecal sludge management and toilet design, the Clean and Green Programme, and the Community-Based Waste Management and Open Defecation Control Programme. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. Lawal announced that the ministry would convene a National Dialogue on Faecal Sludge Management on November 23, 2026, involving seven selected states across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the dialogue would enable participating states to assess their experiences, share challenges and develop practical recommendations for improving faecal sludge management. item.title: MOSOP accuses Niger Delta governors of mismanaging 13% derivation funds
item.description: ….Group calls for amendment of derivation law, commends NDDC’s development efforts By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) has accused successive governors in the Niger Delta of mismanaging the 13 per cent derivation funds, calling for an amendment of the law to ensure that oil-producing communities directly benefit from the revenue. MOSOP President, Fegalo Nsuke, made the call on Tuesday in Port Harcourt during activities marking the 31st anniversary of the execution of environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni leaders by the military government of the late General Sani Abacha. Nsuke said the objectives of the derivation fund had not been achieved because state governors allegedly exercised excessive discretion over its allocation, rather than directing the resources to communities where oil and gas were extracted. He argued that the sacrifices of Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni martyrs would have limited impact on the lives of people unless laws governing resource benefits specifically addressed the needs of communities bearing the consequences of oil exploration. “The idea of derivation funds was to address the underdevelopment in the Niger Delta region. However, the structure of administration of the funds makes it vulnerable to abuse and has left the funds at the discretion of state governors. This needs to be addressed,” he said. According to Nsuke, the intention behind the derivation arrangement was to address underdevelopment in oil-producing areas, but the funds were not being adequately directed towards those communities. Citing Ogba/Egbema and Andoni communities in Rivers State, he said areas responsible for significant oil production had yet to receive what he considered adequate development funding. He argued that allowing governors to determine spending priorities without directly channelling an appropriate share to oil-producing communities had undermined the objectives of the derivation arrangement. Commends NDDC Despite his criticism of the management of derivation funds, Nsuke commended the current management of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) for what he described as its visible development impact across the region. He urged the commission to sustain and expand its interventions, noting that the agency emerged from the struggles for justice and development championed by Saro-Wiwa and other Niger Delta activists. “It is important that the areas from where resources are extracted should get their due rewards and a proportionate injection of the derivation funds. The structure for the administration of the derivation funds needs to change if we must achieve that. “I am pleased that the NDDC under its present management is making some impressive impacts. MOSOP will encourage them to do more,” he said. item.title: Troops rescue three kidnap victims, kill two terrorists in Adamawa
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have rescued three kidnapped civilians and killed two terrorists in separate operations in Adamawa State. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, ammunition, locally fabricated explosive devices, stolen vehicles and farm produce belonging to residents who narrowly escaped abduction. The Acting Media Information Officer of OPHK, Capt. Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. He said the three victims were rescued by troops deployed in Mubi following a distress call from farmers around Dutse-Uku in Mubi South Local Government Area. According to him, suspected kidnappers abducted a farmer, identified as Happiness Dama Dauda, on November 9 while she was working on her farm and also stole her motorcycle. Goni said the troops, working with local hunters, mobilised to the area and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their victim and flee. He added that a sustained pursuit led to the rescue of two other residents suspected to have been abducted earlier, bringing the number of rescued victims to three. The troops also recovered a motorcycle, a tricycle conveying 15 bags of beans and a Hi-Jet pickup carrying 13 bags of groundnuts belonging to other farmers who narrowly escaped abduction. Goni said the respective village heads identified the recovered items, which were subsequently handed over to their owners. Two terrorists killed in Gombi In a separate operation on November 8, troops deployed at Zangula Kilba Junction in Gombi Local Government Area foiled an attempted attack by suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists. Two terrorists were killed during the encounter, while others fled following what the military described as the troops’ superior combat readiness and tactical resilience. Items recovered from the fleeing insurgents included two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 115 rounds of ammunition, three belts of empty ammunition links and two cases of locally fabricated explosive devices. Other recovered items included a pair of desert boots, a backpack, an Android phone, a wristwatch and N15,000. Goni said troops had commenced exploitation operations to track down the fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. He added that troops were maintaining aggressive patrols and surveillance across the affected areas to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety. The military urged residents to provide timely and credible intelligence to security agencies, stressing that collaboration between troops and local communities remained critical to tackling terrorism and other security threats. Operation Hadin Kai reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining operational pressure on terrorists and their collaborators to deny them the freedom to threaten the security and livelihoods of residents across the North-East. item.title: Madonna University: 15 nursing students beg for expulsion reversal over TikTok video
item.description: By Chioma Okoye Fifteen nursing students of Madonna University, Nigeria, have appealed to the university management to reverse their expulsion over a controversial TikTok video recorded during their community posting, pleading for another opportunity to complete their studies. The students, in a letter dated November 2, 2026, tendered an unreserved apology to the management, admitting that their conduct was unethical and had brought disrepute to the nursing profession and the university community. The video, which went viral on social media, sparked widespread reactions and prompted disciplinary action by the university management. In the appeal addressed to the university management through the Registrar, the students said they had reflected deeply on their actions and were genuinely remorseful. “We sincerely regret our said actions and assure the University Management and all relevant authorities that such an incident will not repeat itself again,” they said. They pleaded with the management to reconsider its decision, stressing that their families had made significant sacrifices to support their education and enable them to reach the present stage of their academic journey. The students said reversing the expulsion would give them an opportunity to complete their programmes and pursue their chosen professional careers instead of having their academic aspirations cut short. They also appreciated the university management for engaging with their parents and guardians and allowing them to present their concerns. According to the students, they did not take the gesture for granted and remained grateful for the opportunity given to their families to be heard. The appeal, jointly signed by the 15 students, urged the university management to reconsider the punishment and give them a second chance. item.title: Tinubu’s achievements will make it difficult to unseat him – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says it will be immensely difficult for opposition parties to unseat President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. Wike said this in Abuja on Tuesday, after inspecting some ongoing projects within the federal capital territory. He cited what he described as Tinubu’s undeniable and rich report card of infrastructure development across the country. The minister said that the volume and pace of visible achievements delivered under Tinubu’s administration left very little room for political detractors to challenge the ruling party’s record. “You can see clearly that it will be difficult to unseat the president today because the report card is obvious in terms of what he has done. “Like I told you, this is our campaign. People ask what we are going to campaign with, but we have so many visible achievements all around us. “There is no way residents of Abuja will see the kind of infrastructure we have provided and say they are not happy with the achievements of Mr President. It is second to none,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the minister inspected the ongoing construction of Innet Southern Motorway, from the Area 1 roundabout to the Games Village bridges and Southern Parkway, linking Oladipo Diya Road with Ring Road II. He also inspected the ongoing construction of the Arterial Road S1 project in Abuja to connect Ring Road II to the FCT Fire Service Station in the Kaura and Gaduwa district corridors. Highlighting the rapid speed of execution on several key projects in the territory, Wike referenced the rapid transformation of the Southern Parkway project, which was flagged during the celebration of Tinubu’s third year in office. “Within six to seven months, you can see what has been achieved. “It is unimaginable, and that is why we are very happy,” Wike said. He pledged that the FCT administration remained on track to inaugurate at least 10 high-impact projects before the general elections scheduled for Jan. 16, 2027. item.title: Zamfara APC crisis deepens as aspirant petitions NEC, security agencies
item.description: …Yilwatda dismisses allegations as unfounded By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The crisis in the Zamfara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has taken a fresh turn, following a petition by an aspirant to the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), National Working Committee (NWC) and security agencies over the composition of a committee to conduct a court-ordered fresh primary election. The primary is for the Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency following an order by the Court of Appeal. The aspirant, Honourable Hassan Umar Dangaladima, accused the party’s National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, of unilaterally constituting the committee without involving the NWC. He alleged that the committee’s composition raised concerns about its impartiality and called on the party leadership to review the arrangement before the fresh primary. In the petition, Dangaladima claimed that no NWC meeting was convened to deliberate on or approve the committee’s composition and that neither the aspirants nor the Zamfara State chapter and other relevant stakeholders were consulted. However, Yilwatda, through his Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communication, Abimbola Tooki, dismissed the allegations as unfounded. He said the claims did not reflect the party’s established decision-making process, insisting that the NWC operated as a collective body. “The National Chairman does not operate in isolation. He works in consultation and collaboration with other members of the NWC, and decisions are taken collectively in accordance with the party’s constitution, established procedures and internal mechanisms,” Tooki said. He described the suggestion that Yilwatda single-handedly constituted the committee without the knowledge or involvement of the NWC as misleading. According to him, the APC remains committed to respecting the rule of law, implementing court directives and ensuring that its internal processes are transparent, fair and credible. “The APC is a democratic institution governed by rules and collective responsibility, not the personal preferences of any individual,” he said. Alleges committee bias Dangaladima, however, maintained that the committee’s composition raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest. He alleged that some members were loyalists, supporters or agents of another aspirant, Honourable Aminu Sani Jaji, whom he described as his main rival in the contest. The petitioner also challenged Jaji’s eligibility, alleging that his name was not contained in the APC membership register for Birnin Magaji Ward submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said he obtained a Certified True Copy of the register from INEC, which he attached to his petition as evidence. Dangaladima further claimed that the party had been formally notified of the alleged membership irregularity through a letter dated November 4, 2026, from his solicitors, Trinity Chambers, led by D.C. item.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. item.title: UK, Nigeria seal $750m infrastructure deal as Pension funds prepare to unlock billions
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria and the United Kingdom have strengthened their economic partnership with a proposed $750 million infrastructure investment fund aimed at mobilising billions of dollars in pension assets to finance critical development projects across Nigeria and other selected African markets. The initiative, which has already attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, is expected to channel long-term domestic and international investments into key sectors, including energy, transportation and digital infrastructure, as both countries seek to address the continent’s widening infrastructure financing gap. A statement from PenCom disclosed that the agreement was signed by Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC,and UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, in Lagos on November 10, 2026. Under the agreement, FSD Africa will provide technical expertise and advisory support to PILC towards establishing the proposed investment platform, including the selection of a fund manager through a competitive process, engagement with prospective investors and development finance institutions, capacity building and support for necessary regulatory reforms. The initiative was developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators, PFAs, with support from the National Pension Commission, PenCom, and FSD Africa. Speaking on the development, UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said the partnership reflected the shared commitment of both countries to mobilising domestic capital, particularly pension funds, for productive investment in the real economy. According to him: “The UK is proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment. Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. It is great to see Nigeria making concrete progress on its efforts and be a part of those opportunities to turn this ambition into investment, jobs, and economic growth.” On her part, Chair of the Nigeria Pension Industry Leadership Council and Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, described the proposed investment platform as timely, stressing that the pension industry was committed to deploying its substantial pool of long-term savings towards national development while protecting contributors’ retirement funds. She said: “The pension industry holds the largest pool of long-term savings capital in the country, and we are committed to mobilising it to deepen infrastructure development, while safeguarding the retirement savings of contributors. item.title: Ologe highlights growing importance of risk leadership in digital business
item.description: Mojisola Ologe, an Associate Chartered Risk Manager, has highlighted the growing importance of risk management in strengthening corporate governance, business performance and operational resilience amid increasing digitalisation. Ologe, who received the professional designation from the Chartered Risk Management Institute of Nigeria (CRMI) on October 15, 2026, said effective risk management was becoming increasingly important as organisations expanded their reliance on technology and digital services. She noted that decisions involving access to information systems, introduction of new services, third-party dependencies and business recovery arrangements could have direct implications for customers, regulatory compliance and organisational credibility. Her professional experience spans consulting, banking and digital payments, including roles at Phillips Consulting and Sterling Bank, where she worked across technology assurance, information technology risk and control, business continuity and compliance oversight. The experience, according to her, has reinforced the need to translate identified operational and technological weaknesses into practical business implications and corrective actions. Ologe currently serves as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer at Hydrogen Payment Services Limited, where her responsibilities cover enterprise risk management, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity governance and operational resilience. In the digital payments sector, these areas are closely interconnected, as disruptions to technology systems can quickly affect customer services, expose businesses to financial losses and create regulatory challenges. Effective risk management, therefore, goes beyond identifying potential threats to understanding business operations, assessing critical dependencies and ensuring that management takes timely corrective action. Clear accountability, appropriate internal controls and effective escalation mechanisms are also essential to helping organisations address vulnerabilities while pursuing their business objectives. Ologe’s professional recognition by CRMI underscores the importance of continuous professional development in the risk management sector, particularly as emerging technologies and changing business conditions create new operational and regulatory challenges. Risk professionals, increasingly, are expected to contribute beyond compliance monitoring by providing insights that inform corporate strategy, investment decisions and everyday business operations. Their role, the profile noted, is to help organisations pursue growth while maintaining a clear understanding of potential exposures and strengthening their capacity to withstand disruptions. item.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. In November 2025, he chaired a hearing after President Donald Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a ‘country of particular concern’. In May 2016, he also chaired a hearing on “The U.S. role in helping Nigeria confront Boko Haram and other threats in northern Nigeria.” The post US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation. Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. item.title: Wenger considers challenging Infantino for FIFA presidency — Report
item.description: Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering a challenge against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, according to the BBC. The 77-year-old Frenchman is giving serious thought to contesting the position following growing calls from influential figures in European football for him to enter the race. Some of Wenger’s supporters have reportedly indicated that they would back him even if he chose to step down before completing the four-year presidential term. His possible candidacy could pose a significant challenge to Infantino, whose leadership has faced criticism following the collapse of a plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Although the controversy has unsettled his position in parts of European football, Infantino retains considerable support in South America, Africa and Asia. He recently maintained that he enjoys the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of the global football community. Wenger, who currently serves as Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development, is expected to enjoy the backing of the Union of European Football Associations (Uefa), which has led opposition to Infantino over the abandoned commercial proposal. However, sources close to the Frenchman told BBC Sport that he has yet to make a final decision on whether to contest the election. They also believe Infantino remains the favourite to secure another term. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to challenge Infantino is November 18, ahead of the election scheduled for March. Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega became the first candidate to announce his intention to run in October, while Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also indicated interest in the position. item.title: Why I rejected US asylum offer before Abacha arrested me — Obasanjo
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has revealed that he rejected an offer of political asylum from the United States despite being warned that he would be arrested if he returned to Nigeria under the late military Head of State, Gen. Sani Abacha. Obasanjo also recounted how he ventured into farming after retiring from the Nigerian Army at 42. The former president disclosed this while narrating his experience under the military government in an interview published by BBC News Pidgin on Tuesday. He said, “When I was leaving government as military head of state, I was leaving too early. I didn’t join the army to retire at the age of 42. “Now I had to retire at the age of 42. At the age of 42, I had become a four-star general. There’s nothing else I can do in the army. I’ve become the military head of state. That’s the highest political office I could rise. Obasanjo said his farming business was progressing well until Abacha’s government moved against him. He said he rejected the US asylum because he had committed no crime. “So what can I do? I decided I would go into farming. It really was going well, and it went well until I was arrested. “Abacha had decided that I must be liquidated; otherwise he would not be able to have his way. I didn’t know that. I was travelling and coming back, and the American ambassador in Nigeria called me and said his country had offered me political asylum because they knew that I would be arrested if I returned home. “This was difficult for me. I don’t— I haven’t done anything. What do they want to arrest me for? Um, I don’t want political asylum.” He said his passport was later seized, after which he proceeded to his farm. On arrival, one of his security personnel informed him that government security operatives had surrounded the premises. According to him, a police officer dressed in civilian clothes subsequently approached him, claiming that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) had invited him. “And when I arrived, they seized my passport; I made for my farm. At the gate of my farm was my security. He waved me down. He said that security had surrounded the farm. And within 15 minutes, this man came in mufti, not in uniform, a policeman, and he said, ‘Well, you have been invited by the AIG to come and help him.’ I said, ‘You are a fool.’ “‘If the AIG wants me to help him, he will not be inviting me. He will come here,” Obasanjo lamented, adding, “So it was my own car that I used to take myself to the police station. We saw the AIG, and the AIG said, ‘I have been instructed to arrest you.’” The former president also disclosed that former United States President Jimmy Carter intervened on his behalf by appealing to Abacha. item.title: US Judge Orders Psychiatric Exam For Meghan Markle’s Father
item.description: A US judge has ordered a psychiatric examination for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan Markle, after his arrest for alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse. Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of “possession of child pornography” and made an initial court appearance in Tampa in Florida on Friday. Judge Lindsay Griffin cited his “health condition,” “advanced age” and “lack of recall” in the order issued on Friday, without providing further details. Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents earlier that day at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida. The Justice Department said he allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades.” File photo of Meghan and Thomas Markle Pictures of child sex abuse have also allegedly been found at Markle’s former home in the Philippines and at a storage unit he rented in Mexico. The judge said she found “reasonable cause to believe” that Markle was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.” She instructed a psychiatrist to provide a report on Markle’s mental state by November 20. The judge permitted Markle to be moved to house arrest with electronic monitoring, CNN reported. Markle had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the United States this year. Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse. He could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. item.title: ‘I didn’t tell them to go buy votes,’ Wike defends N10m reward for councillors
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said he never asked councillors to buy votes with the N10 million he promised those who deliver their wards in the 2027 general elections. “I didn’t tell them, ‘Take this money and go and buy votes.’ I said, ‘Go and work. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come, and we are going to reward you,” he said. Wike spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects in Abuja. He was responding to criticism of the promise, which he said was an incentive for hard work and not an attempt to buy votes. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali Area Council the previous day, Wike had explained that the initiative was part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “For the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again, and I will now say the way I am going to mobilise you, but I will give you a bet, like what is happening in the stars; it’s a competition. “Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward, that is what the Rainbow Coalition has decided to do as mobilisation and support for Mr President; we have to start in the FCT (I couldn’t say so when the president came because they gave me only two minutes to talk). But now that I have time to talk, let me say that the Rainbow Coalition all over the federation, as a form of mobilisation for Mr President to win this election, is saying that any councillor that delivers his ward will come and take N10 million. We want to mobilise for Mr President. So, go to your wards, and go and see your leaders. I know only you cannot do it, but we are using you as an instrumentality for your leaders. Go and meet your leaders and say, ‘Look, oh, there is something that has come.’ We must not allow this thing to go. Let’s dedicate our ward for Mr President’. So, that is for that,” Wike had said. Speaking on Tuesday, Wike drew a line between rewarding political commitment and offering money to voters in exchange for their support. He said the councillors were challenged to prove their commitment through effective mobilisation. To make his case, he pointed to athletes who are promised houses or other benefits if they return from international competitions with trophies. He asked why a similar reward in politics should automatically be read as bribery. He also faulted sections of the media for failing to tell legitimate rewards apart from vote-buying. Political parties and candidates, he argued, routinely spend money on campaign advertisements without facing the same scrutiny. Wike urged journalists to pay closer attention to the difference between financial inducements meant to sway voters and rewards promised to political mobilisers for hitting set targets. item.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
item.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. item.title: CAF reschedules 2026 Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has rescheduled the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos. CAF announced the new date in a statement on Tuesday, with the event brought forward five days. Although the football body gave no reason for the change, the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Art Theatre, in Lagos, remains the venue for the ceremony. The event will mark the return of the CAF Awards to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition, bringing together leading players, coaches, clubs and other personalities in African football to celebrate their achievements. A total of 18 categories will be recognised at the ceremony, with the CAF Men’s Player of the Year and CAF Women’s Player of the Year awards among the major honours. Other categories will recognise outstanding coaches, goalkeepers, emerging talents, clubs and national teams for their performances during the year. Meanwhile, voting for the 2026 awards is ongoing and will run from November 5 to 20 across the men’s and women’s categories.
